note: A trace of the requirement rows in the 2026-11-17 brief, each checked against this repository's tree rather than taken from the brief's own status word. Placeholder tokens in the data (named after what they count) are replaced by tools/build_board.py with a value it MEASURES from the tree in the same run, and tools/validate_board.py re-measures and fails if any printed number disagrees. That is the whole point: this repository has twice shipped a page whose prose printed a count that had drifted from the register it described (FB-01, FB-02, and the two defects the T57 live read-back caught), and a typed count in this file would be a third.

verdict_vocabulary.matches: the tree supports the status word the brief gives it
verdict_vocabulary.overstated: the tree shows less than the brief's status word claims
verdict_vocabulary.as-stated: the brief records a decision rather than a measurement; this namespace does not re-open it
verdict_vocabulary.no-status-given: the brief left the status cell empty, so there is nothing to agree or disagree with — only a measurement to supply
verdict_vocabulary.unmeasurable-from-the-tree: the row describes an outcome in the world, not an artefact in the repository

rows.requirement: Give every page its own title and meta description
rows.measured: {{unique_titles}} distinct titles across {{pages}} published pages; {{no_desc}} pages carry no meta description and {{dup_desc}} descriptions are shared by more than one page; {{dup_titles}} titles are shared by more than one page.
rows.evidence: Measured by tools/build_board.py across every published .html file, and enforced from 2026-11-19 by D8 in tools/seo_audit.py (a CI step) with negative controls in tests/test_page_identity.py. T72 closed the row at its generators rather than in the output: the 7 blank pages were the 404 page and all six revalidation/ pages (revalidation/scripts/build.py plus 404.html), the 39 identical pages/ descriptions and 4 identical decisions/ descriptions were a single HUB_DESCRIPTION string printed by tools/build_site.py and tools/build_decisions.py, and the duplicated titles were the two category bands, pages/niches.html vs the M-11 module page, and both thermometer pages. Every replacement is derived from text the page already published (its own <h1> and standfirst), so no new claim was introduced.
rows.gap: None remaining. D8 fails the build if any of the three properties regresses.

rows.requirement: Mark the affiliate links rel="sponsored" without breaking the required disclosure
rows.measured: {{amazon_links}} outbound links to an Amazon host across the tree, of which {{sponsored_links}} carry rel="sponsored". On the {{reader_pages}} reader-facing pages the split is {{sponsored_reader}} sponsored against {{unsponsored_reader}} not — and every unsponsored one of those sits on a register page (verification, sources, summary, paths, questions), citing the URL as evidence rather than offering the product for sale.
rows.evidence: BD-15 defines the value by what the link is: 'Mark links that are advertisements or paid placements (commonly called paid links) with the sponsored value.' A citation to a source page inside a verification table is neither.
rows.gap: None on this row. The related gap is RQ-22: the links are correctly marked as sponsored and still carry no Associates tag, so they are marked but not monetised.

rows.requirement: Add the one thing a listing cannot tell a reader: what the appliance is like to live with
rows.brief_status: Not adopted - see the recorded decision
rows.measured: No first-hand use review exists on any page. The site's stated position is that it reports what official pages say and leaves the rest blank.
rows.evidence: The brief records this as decided against, with the decision linked as D-06. This namespace does not re-open another session's recorded decision.
rows.gap: Recorded, not open. It is listed here only because the two new products change its cost: a first-hand review of a thermometer is a different and cheaper piece of work than a first-hand review of a 26-quart oven, so the decision may be worth revisiting for the two new items specifically.

rows.gap: The one-page-per-question shape is in place for all five products. What the row asks — the questions people actually type — cannot be selected from measured queries until Search Console or another first-party query source is on (see RQ-19, RQ-28). rows.requirement: Ship a social preview image and structured data, then measure whether search traffic arrives
rows.measured_status: partly — preview metadata is present on a subset; Search Console remains off
rows.measured: {{jsonld}} of {{pages}} pages carry JSON-LD. {{og_full}} of {{pages}} carry og:type, og:site_name, og:title, og:description and og:url. {{og_image}} of {{pages}} carry an og:image. {{sc_pages}} of {{pages}} carry a Search Console verification tag.

rows.requirement: Mobile-first pass: type scale, tap targets, sticky comparison bar
rows.measured: {{viewport_pages}} of {{pages}} pages declare a viewport. The phone-only sticky comparison bar (.cn-sticky-compare) sits on compare.html. At a 390 px headless-Chromium viewport the 64 reader pages plus all 17 shop/ pages and root compare.html, shop.html, about.html and privacy.html (85 pages total) show 0 text-bearing elements under 11 px and 0 standalone targets with either dimension under 24 CSS px (before: 455 and 1,900 under the same method).
rows.evidence: Measured on 2026-11-19 in headless Chromium 153.0.8010.0 at 390x844 over the 85-page reader/shop sign-off set; method, 2,030-target 24-44 px band classification and official W3C criterion links are in docs/verification-5a3dd862.md.
rows.gap: Signed off 2026-11-19 (T76), completing T72's partial pass (PR #193). Type floor: text-bearing elements below 11 px raised to 11 px at 780 px and below in all four reader stylesheets (marketing.css, style.css, publish.css, shop.css), desktop unchanged. Tap targets: all standalone reader-scope targets measured at least 24x24 CSS px (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 size branch, Level AA); inline links in sentences are separately classified under its Inline exception. Prominent header/footer/top-nav links have a 44 px minimum height; this is not a claim that all such links meet the 44x44 AAA target. The remaining 2,030 targets below 44 px comprise 1,318 source/reference chips, 222 other table-cell links, 220 header/navigation/footer links and 270 other section/card/content links and controls; every one measures at least 24x24 CSS px. See docs/verification-5a3dd862.md for the explicit classification and caveats. Operator/admin namespaces remain out of scope. The sticky comparison bar and disclosure-above-fold checks run in tests/browser.cjs; the new 390 px text-floor assertion covers the reader pages.
